## Map of NYC Parks by Borough 

```{r message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)

parks_raw <- read_csv("data/Parks_Properties_20251104.csv")

parks_sf <-
  parks_raw |>
  st_as_sf(wkt = "multipolygon", crs = 4326) |> 
  mutate(
    borough_name = dplyr::recode(
      BOROUGH,
      "M" = "Manhattan",
      "B" = "Brooklyn",
      "Q" = "Queens",
      "X" = "Bronx",
      "R" = "Staten Island")
    )

pal <-
  colorFactor(
    palette = "viridis",  
    domain  = parks_sf$borough_name
    )

leaflet(parks_sf) |>
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor   = ~pal(borough_name),
    color       = "transparent",
    weight      = 1,
    fillOpacity = 1,
    smoothFactor = 0.2,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color  = "white",
      bringToFront = TRUE),
    label = ~paste0(SIGNNAME, " (", borough_name, ")"),
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<strong>", SIGNNAME, "</strong><br/>",
      "Borough: ", borough_name, "<br/>",
      "Acres: ", ACRES)
    ) |>
  addLegend(
    "bottomright",
    pal    = pal,
    values = ~borough_name,
    title  = "Borough",
    opacity = 0.5
    )
```

Built using data from [NYC Parks Propety dataset](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Recreation/Parks-Properties-Map/krz2-j7bn) from NYC Open Data 

___
## About Our Project

**Does having more park space in your community actually relate to better health?**

Using NYC Parks data and the NYC Community Health Profiles, we explored how park access connects to two outcomes: premature mortality and adult obesity. Along the way, we dug into patterns across boroughs, cleaned and merged a lot of data, and ran models to see what matters most.

Short answer? Park access matters, but it's only one piece of a much bigger picture about neighborhood health.

Explore the site to see what we discovered!
